name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about nineteen points Republican, anchoring the race to the incumbent's advantage
Glenn Thompson holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge over Ray Bilger with no meaningful outside spending in the race
No public polls or expert ratings track the contest, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a four percent win probability
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Thompson's long incumbency, and his overwhelming financial advantage leave little realistic path for Bilger; markets and fundamentals align on a comfortable Republican hold, with even a favorable national environment for Democrats unlikely to close a nineteen-point gap.
model.watch: A decisive national Democratic wave or an unexpected scandal involving Thompson could tighten the race, though nothing in the current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 15th District is a heavily Republican rural seat in the north-central part of the state, represented by Glenn Thompson since 2009. The district's partisan lean of roughly nineteen points toward Republicans forms the foundation of this race, and Thompson enters the general election as a clear favorite over Democrat Ray Bilger.

Thompson has out-raised Bilger by about ten to one and holds a large cash-on-hand advantage, with essentially no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings follow the contest, and prediction markets give Bilger only about a four percent chance of an upset. Even accounting for a national environment that favors Democrats this cycle, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Thompson win, with the real uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
